uncited: It builds on [Mesh/Point Cloud Evaluation Metrics](4797-mesh-point-cloud-evaluation-metrics.md) but restricts the comparison domain to the viewing frusta of the input cameras.
- Reconstructed mesh $M_{rec}$ (triangle soup or manifold mesh).
- Ground truth mesh $M_{gt}$ (optional, depending on metric; primarily used for visibility definition in this specific pipeline context, though IoU/F-score often compare $M_{rec}$ to $M_{gt}$).
- Camera poses $P_i$ (extrinsics) and intrinsics $K_i$ for all input frames $i=1 \dots N$.
- Input color/depth streams (used to define the "visible" domain).
- Scalar metrics: $C_{\ell1}$, IoU, NC, F-score.
- Point cloud $S_{rec}$: Set of 3D points sampled from $M_{rec}$.
- Point cloud $S_{gt}$: Set of 3D points sampled from $M_{gt}$ (or voxel grid centers).
- Voxel grid $V_{rec}$: Binary occupancy grid for $M_{rec}$.
- Voxel grid $V_{gt}$: Binary occupancy grid for $M_{gt}$.
This ensures uniform sampling density and accurate visibility detection.
- For each vertex $v$ in the subdivided $M_{rec}$, project it into the image plane of each input camera $i$ using $P_i$ and $K_i$.
- A triangle is **visible** if at least one of its vertices is visible.

- Similarly, sample points from the corresponding visible regions of the ground truth mesh $M_{gt}$ (or the entire $M_{gt}$ if the metric definition implies global comparison, but the text implies evaluation on surfaces visible in streams) to form $S_{gt}$.

*Note: The source specifies evaluating metrics on surfaces visible in input streams, implying $S_{gt}$ should also be restricted to visible regions or the comparison is strictly between visible reconstructions and their corresponding visible GT.*
*(Note: Source specifies $C_{\ell1}$, which usually implies L1 norm, but Chamfer is often L2.
Let $V_{rec}$ and $V_{gt}$ be the resulting voxel sets.
- Calculate precision: fraction of voxels in $V_{rec}$ that have a neighbor in $V_{gt}$ within distance $\tau$.
- Calculate recall: fraction of voxels in $V_{gt}$ that have a neighbor in $V_{rec}$ within distance $\tau$.
- **Time Complexity**: Dominated by visibility testing ($O(V \cdot N)$ where $V$ is vertices, $N$ is frames) and nearest-neighbor searches for metrics ($O(|S_{rec}| \log |S_{gt}|)$).
Subdivision adds overhead proportional to mesh complexity.
- **Memory Complexity**: Linear in the number of vertices and sampled points.
Voxelization requires memory proportional to the scene volume divided by $L_{vox}^3$.
If visibility is incorrectly determined, valid geometry may be culled or invalid geometry retained.
The choice of $L_{max}$ and sampling density affects precision.
- **When not to use**: When evaluating scene completion or methods that explicitly predict hidden geometry.
It addresses the limitation of standard mesh metrics by acknowledging that reconstruction methods are typically trained only on visible geometry.
